newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Santander Investment cuts Colombian GDP forecast.
newsitem.headline: Santander Investment cuts Colombian GDP forecast.

text.p: Santander Investment said it cut its estimate of real economic growth in Colombia this year from 3.0 percent to 2.5 percent.
"We have downgraded our real GDP growth estimate to 2.5 percent from 3.0 percent," the bank said in a statement.

"In the first half of 1996, GDP grew at an annualized rate of 3.0 percent. We expect the downward trend to continue through year-end, before picking up again in 1997, when we anticipate 3.5 percent growth," it said.
Colombia's private economic think-tank Fedesarrollo is predicting that the country's gross domestic product will grow by 3.1 percent in 1996, down from official goverment estimates of 3.5 percent.
Fedesarollo sees GDP growth of 4.5 percent in 1997 against government estimates of 5.2 percent.
